name: Basilica of St. Fidelis
history: The parish of Victoria built St. Fidelis between 1908 and 1911. By parish history, every member aged 12 or older was asked to give $45 and haul six wagonloads of Fencepost limestone and four of sand each year until it was done. It was named a basilica in 2014.
arch: Romanesque Revival in local Fencepost limestone, designed by John T. Comès of Pittsburgh and supervised by Joseph Marshall of Topeka. Its twin towers are 141 feet tall.
features: William Jennings Bryan, visiting in 1912, gave it the nickname "the Cathedral of the Plains".
Its 48 stained glass windows, installed in 1916 for $3,700, are now valued at over $1 million.

look.d: Visible from Interstate 70, a landmark of western Kansas.
Parishioners carted the limestone themselves, wagon by wagon.

fun: It is not a cathedral at all; the nickname came from William Jennings Bryan.
journal: Prairie limestone hauled by hand. A cathedral in everything but title.
